linesVerbatim: ## Common component packaging and language build adapters
**Proposed V2 architecture model.** Every OpenSIP component release, regardless
of implementation language, emits one common packaging/admission contract:
- a canonical closed manifest and stable component/release identity;
- immutable archive and full-tree path/type/mode/length/digest commitment,
including entrypoint and required runtime/tool bytes;
- signed publisher provenance plus bound SBOM, attestation, license, and notice
inventory;
- explicit supported-platform alternatives and per-surface compatibility;
- declared capabilities, prerequisites, permissions, state/migration, and
capability/performance parity evidence;
- static validation, health, and role/subprotocol conformance results;
- signed offline/air-gap installation inputs;
- deterministic update, rollback, repair, and revocation metadata; and
- download/install/startup/memory and role-quality gate evidence.
Language runtimes and ecosystems differ, so per-language **build adapters** may
use different internal build mechanisms. Each adapter is responsible for
collecting and normalizing its language's runtime/parser/compiler/language-server
closure into the same OpenSIP output contract. Variation ends at the adapter
boundary: admission, signing, exact-byte verification, lifecycle, offline use,
and measurement consume the common contract rather than language-specific
package-manager semantics.
DR-120 must define the adapter template and developer ergonomics: deterministic
and hermetic CI inputs, reproducible local validation, actionable missing-field
diagnostics, fixture generation, platform fan-out, and one conformance report
shape. Acceptance tests cover clean install, no ambient dependencies, hostile
paths, health/subprotocol negotiation, offline/air-gap use, update/rollback, and
all relevant size/quality/performance gates.
This architecture does not choose a concrete packager, build tool, language
toolchain, or command line. Those choices belong in `docs/v2/implementation/`
after DR-120 is accepted and blueprint work is authorized.

outputContract.discipline: Every component release, regardless of implementation language, emits one common packaging/admission contract. This artifact names the members and the adapter's emission duty. Admission, uniqueness, path, signature-byte, and closure refusals are owned by component-manifest-schemas.v2 (D-013). This artifact does not fork those schemas.

consumes.relation: Emission target. Adapters MUST emit bytes that are structurally valid against that contract's manifest/index/lock field rules. They MUST NOT invent a parallel manifest dialect.

members.name: canonical closed manifest and stable identity
members.emits: A standalone manifest document (kind: component) with required stableId, name, version, role, commands, capabilities, platforms, dependencies, declarations, permissions, provenance, reserved stateMigration, reserved updateData, and compatibility.
members.adapterDuty: Populate every required field from the language build. Do not derive stableId from a package-manager name. Do not execute the component to discover identity.

members.name: immutable archive and full-tree commitment
members.emits: Per-platform TreeCommitment (path/type/mode/length/digest) including entrypoint and every required runtime/tool byte. No Merkle root (ID-DEP-3 reserved).
members.ownedBy: DR-103 treeCommitmentShape; exact-byte delivery in file 04
members.adapterDuty: Collect the language runtime/parser/compiler/language-server (or analog) into the tree. Refuse ambient PATH/system-runtime/project-package-manager resolution as a substitute for a tree entry (D-008).

members.name: signed publisher provenance plus bound SBOM/attestation/license/notice
members.emits: provenance object plus declarations.licenses/sbom/attestation digest refs, or typed absence under an approved exception. Detached signature envelope is a binding point; ceremony is DR-112.
members.adapterDuty: Bind declaration bytes into the signed closure. Do not embed a signature field in the manifest. Do not invent envelope/key/threshold semantics.

members.name: supported-platform alternatives and per-surface compatibility
members.emits: platforms[] over the slice-1 vocabulary (macos/arm64, macos/x86_64, linux/x86_64, linux/arm64) and a compatibility object whose VALUES are data. Window meaning is DR-111's.
members.adapterDuty: Fan out one emission per supported platform alternative. Do not evaluate version windows. Do not invent a Windows platform entry (D-002).

members.name: capabilities, prerequisites, permissions, state/migration, parity evidence
members.emits: capabilities[] (may be empty), optional prerequisites only in the D-008 approved-exception shape, permissions[] as requested tokens only, reserved stateMigration, and declarations.capabilityParityEvidence / performanceBaseline.
members.ownedBy: DR-103; DR-105 token vocabulary (ID-DEP-11); DR-124/106/109/113 for stateMigration
members.adapterDuty: Declare requested permissions; never grant. Populate stateMigration only as the reserved marker. Do not mint permission tokens.

members.name: static validation, health, and role/subprotocol conformance results
members.emits: A conformance-report document (conformanceReport) recording static validation of the emission, health-probe applicability, and the opaque roleSubprotocol / subprotocolVersion tokens. No framing, negotiation, or translation.
members.ownedBy: This artifact for the report shape; DR-102 for negotiation semantics
members.adapterDuty: Record results. Do not negotiate. Do not translate provider frames.

members.name: signed offline/air-gap installation inputs
members.emits: The exact set file 04 names as air-gap input: signed index snapshot, manifests, payloads, permissions, plus reserved slots for root chain / last-known revocation / expiry / repair material owned by DR-112/DR-110.
members.ownedBy: DR-103 index/lock; DR-112/110 for trust/repair material
members.adapterDuty: Emit the component-local inputs (manifest, tree, declarations, detached-envelope binding). Do not design the trust state machine.

members.name: deterministic update, rollback, repair, and revocation metadata
members.emits: The reserved updateData marker only. Semantics wait on DR-110 and DR-112.
members.adapterDuty: Emit { reserved: true, ridesOn: [DR-110, DR-112] }. Populating the member is RJ-6. Acceptance-test class AT-6 exists as a REQUIREMENT whose vectors wait on those rows, by D-002 symmetry.

members.name: download/install/startup/memory and role-quality gate evidence
members.emits: Digest references to the evidence artifacts those gates consume. Threshold VALUES are D-006 / DR-115 / DR-118's. This artifact binds the binding points, not the numbers.
members.adapterDuty: Declare the evidence paths/digests. Do not invent thresholds. Do not claim QUALIFIED.

adapterTemplate.name: opensip-build-adapter
adapterTemplate.notAPackager: This is a contract a language adapter must satisfy. It is not cargo, npm, esbuild, webpack, a Dockerfile, or a CLI.

stages.does: Collect the language's runtime/parser/compiler/language-server (or analog) and the component's own bytes as a closed input set. Inputs are named, digest-pinned, and networkless.
stages.mustNot: Implicit download. Ambient PATH lookup. Live-project package-manager resolution used as a substitute for collected bytes.

stages.does: Normalize language-specific package-manager shapes (DIFF-7: npm/package.json and analogs remain adapter INPUTS) into the common output-contract members.
stages.mustNot: Let package-manager semantics reach admission, signing, exact-byte verification, lifecycle, offline use, or measurement.

stages.does: Emit the standalone manifest, per-platform tree, declaration artifacts, detached-signature binding point, and conformance report.
stages.mustNot: Execute the component under admission. Embed a signature field. Populate a reserved binding point. Mint a role, permission token, or identity recipe.

stages.does: Run the local developer validation flow (same rules as CI) and emit missing-field diagnostics naming the failed OC member.
stages.mustNot: Apply a weaker local rule than CI. Warn-and-continue. Auto-rename. Silent fallback.

invariants: Variation ends at the adapter boundary (file 02 C-11).
Admission, signing, exact-byte verification, lifecycle, offline use, and measurement consume the common contract only.
Adapter build-time execution of language tools is permitted. Component execution during discovery/admission is forbidden (D-012 clause 7; TC-METADATA-ONLY).
D-008 anti-fallback: never silently substitute a system tool or weaken semantics.
D-008 exception shape is the only lawful unbundled prerequisite.

hermeticCI.discipline: Deterministic and hermetic CI inputs (file 02 C-12).

rules.rule: Every input is named and digest-pinned: source tree, tool closure, adapter version, platform target, exception-approval records if any.
The adapter run is networkless. Any implicit download is RJ-5 plus typed remediation, not a retry.

Identical resolution-class inputs yield identical output-contract tuples (same manifests, same trees, same declaration digests, same report members). Byte-identical archives/manifests ride ID-DEP-1 and are EXPLICITLY conditional until that surface closes.
A missed input, unpinned tool, or dirty worktree is a typed non-success of the adapter run, not a best-effort emission.

localDeveloperValidation.discipline: Reproducible local validation with actionable missing-field diagnostics (file 02 C-12). Same rules as hermeticCI.

rules.rule: Local validation executes the same output-contract checks as CI. A field that fails CI fails locally.
Every failure names exactly one output-contract member (OC-1..OC-9) or exactly one DR-103 refusal family/subcode, plus the missing or malformed path.
Local convenience caches are rebuildable and must not change emission tuples. A cache hit equals recomputation (file 04 rebuildable-cache class).
Local validation does not admit, sign, or publish. It reports. Admission remains the host's DR-103 act.

platformFanOut.discipline: One emission per supported platform alternative declared in platforms[].
platformFanOut.windows: DELIBERATELY absent. D-002 defers Windows. A Windows alternative enters with that platform, not silently before it.
platformFanOut.rule: An adapter that cannot produce a declared platform alternative emits typed unavailability for that alternative. It does not emit a different ISA, a Rosetta stand-in, or a cross-compiled substitute without a distinct platforms[] entry.

conformanceReport.discipline: One conformance report shape (file 02 C-12). No D9 values. No process-exit numbers. No identity recipes.

shape.adapterId: opaque string naming the adapter implementation, not a packager brand requirement
shape.subject: { stableId, version, platform }
shape.outputContractMembers: array of { id: OC-1..OC-9, standing: 'present' | 'typed-absence' | 'reserved' | 'absent', digestOrRef: optional sha256 or path, notes: string }
shape.fixtureClassCoverage: array of { class: TC-* or AT-*, standing: 'produced' | 'not-applicable' | 'blocked-on-ride', ride: optional dependency id }
shape.staticValidation: array of { rule: DR-103 refusal id or OC id, result: 'pass' | 'refuse', code: optional refusal code }
shape.healthAndSubprotocol: opaque tokens only: { roleSubprotocol, subprotocolVersion, healthResultRef }. Negotiation semantics are DR-102's.
shape.exclusionsRecorded: NO secret values, NO user trust decisions, NO self-granted authority, NO D9/exit numbers, NO QUALIFIED/DEMONSTRATED/SATISFIED tokens

idDep8.feature: Producing manifests from language builds; conformance of adapters to the DR-103 schema; fixture generation for the test corpus
idDep8.consequence: component-manifest-schemas.v2 defines the classes. This artifact defines how an adapter produces them. DR-G15 executes adapter × platform × clean/offline/upgrade. Naming DR-G15 does not author fixtures.

generationContract.rule: An adapter MUST be able to emit, from a language build, one fixture for every DR-103 testCorpusRequirements class member that is not conditional or Windows-deferred.
Each generated fixture is digest-pinned per file and states expected outcome ACCEPT or exactly one refusal family/subcode.

Hand-authoring of the exact-byte corpus is lawful evidence that the classes exist. It is not an adapter run. It does not SATISFY DR-103 until independently reviewed at SATISFIED-GRADE and recorded by a later D-000 MF-6. It does not SATISFY DR-120.

The authored candidate at component-manifest-fixture-corpus.v1.json (d81a4ef9…) is cited as that hand-authored evidence. Its review is a separate SATISFIED-GRADE act. This artifact does not inherit that verdict and does not close ID-DEP-8 by citing the file.
Conditional classes (ENVELOPE_MISMATCH; signing-preimage vectors) follow their ID-DEP-1 / ID-DEP-5 dispositions. Ceremony classes belong to DR-112.

acceptanceTests.discipline: These are REQUIREMENT classes. DR-G15 executes them. Existing here does not QUALIFY any adapter.

classes.name: clean install
classes.requires: A generated ACCEPT emission installs on a clean machine from signed offline inputs only. Help/completion/inventory remain metadata-only.

classes.name: no ambient dependencies
classes.requires: Removing PATH, system runtime, and project package-manager state does not change the emission or the clean-install result. An implicit-download attempt is RJ-5 plus typed remediation.

classes.name: hostile paths
classes.requires: Every DR-103 TC-PATH class member that is not Windows-deferred is produced by the adapter or is an authored exact-byte fixture the adapter's validator refuses. Windows-only classes remain absent.

classes.name: health/subprotocol negotiation
classes.requires: The conformance report carries opaque roleSubprotocol/subprotocolVersion tokens. Actual negotiation, framing, and hostile dual-channel classes remain DR-102 / DR-G21. This class proves the adapter emitted the tokens and did not translate frames.

classes.name: offline/air-gap use
classes.requires: The emission plus reserved trust slots is sufficient for a no-network install of that component. Missing reserved trust material is typed unavailability owned by DR-112/110, not a silent success.

classes.name: update/rollback
classes.requires: DECLARED as a class. Vectors are INACTIVE until DR-110 and DR-112 close or dispose. If either closes by scoped disposition, this class follows that disposition's terms (D-002 symmetry). Until then no adapter may emit updateData semantics.

classes.name: size/quality/performance gates
classes.requires: The emission binds evidence paths for DR-G01..G05 / DR-115 / DR-118 / DR-G13. Thresholds and measurement remain those rows. This class proves the binding points exist, not that numbers pass.

cellWordCoverage.discipline: The OBL-5 cell fragment lists properties the fixtures must prove. Each word maps to a DR-103 class, an AT class, or a reserved ride. Absence of an authored DR-120 adapter-generated fixture is honest: FG-3 allows hand-authored exact-byte evidence; DR-G15 executes adapter generation.

representativeLanguageClosures.laterRoles: Additional language adapters reuse this template. They do not reopen OBL-1..OBL-5. They do not require a new DR-120 successor unless the output contract itself changes.

identityDependencies.pattern: Named per the D-002 symmetry-clause pattern: each dependency names the open surface it rides, presumes nothing settled, and if the named surface closes by scoped disposition rather than a binding artifact, the dependent feature here ships reduced, re-scoped, or waits, by that disposition's terms; none of it survives on prose.

dependencies.consequence: Until that surface closes, hermeticCI promises tuple-level identity only. Byte-level identity is conditional.

dependencies.feature: Compatibility window evaluation in emitted constraints
dependencies.consequence: Adapters emit compatibility data. They must not evaluate windows. THIS ARTIFACT PROPOSES that adapters must not emit a lock of any form until DR-111 closes. ATTRIBUTION: the D-013-accepted component-manifest-schemas.v2 (73114dde…) states only that no lock over a constrained request is producible; exact-pin is not a request form in that accepted document. The widening is proposed here (and written in unaccepted schema successors); citing those successors does not accept DR-103 and does not lend D-013's acceptance to the wider rule.

dependencies.feature: Signature envelope ceremony and update/rollback/revocation metadata
dependencies.consequence: OC-8 and AT-6 stay reserved/inactive. Ceremony fixtures are not this corpus.

dependencies.ridesOn: DR-102 (design SATISFIED; execution leftover at DR-G21)
dependencies.consequence: Tokens are opaque here. Negotiation is not redesigned.
UNKNOWN_PERMISSION_TOKEN remains undecidable until the vocabulary is minted. Adapters emit requested tokens only.
stateMigration stays reserved. D-002 defers 106/109/113 wholly for slice 1.

dependencies.feature: Gate threshold values and TypeScript quality corpus
dependencies.consequence: This artifact binds evidence paths. It does not decide numbers or author the language-quality corpus.

dependencies.ridesOn: Independent SATISFIED-GRADE review of component-manifest-fixture-corpus.v1 and a later D-000 MF-6
dependencies.consequence: Citing the authored corpus does not SATISFY DR-103 or close ID-DEP-8.
